newsitem.title: FRANCE: Elf workers at Grandpuits plant renew strike again.
newsitem.headline: Elf workers at Grandpuits plant renew strike again.

text.p: Workers at Elf Aquitaine's Grandpuits refinery voted on Wednesday morning to extend their strike until later in the day, a union official there said.
The refinery has been closed for a week in a dispute with the French oil firm's Elf Antar subsidiary over job cuts.
"It's the same situation. We are carrrying on," the union official told Reuters after a meeting of day workers.
Strikes at two other plants, Feyzin and Donges, are now in their seventh day. They will also be reviewed later on Wednesday.
Union officials predict the strike will continue until at least Thursday, when talks are due.
All Elf's French refining capacity except a tiny stake in a small majority-owned Shell plant in eastern France has been shut down by the strike, which is being renewed on a shift-by-shift basis.

Night shift workers at Grandpuits, near Paris, voted on Tuesday evening to extend their strike after unions described negotiations over pay and other issues set for Thursday as a diversion from the main issue of employment.
Elf said on Tuesday that union representatives and managers from Elf Antar France would meet on Thursday at 1300 GMT to discuss salaries and working organisation and conditions.
It called the negotiation after preliminary talks on Tuesday.
Unions are campaigning for the scrapping of a plan to axe 300 Elf Antar jobs, more pay, shorter hours and retirement at 55 for refinery shift workers.
